There's no inherent fraud or trademark infringement in advertising/bidding for search terms of your competitors. A classic example is Dominos bidding for 'Pizza Hut', and vice versa.

There may be trademark infringement when you use another company's trademarks. There are some exceptions, for example copy like 'Compatible with $X' or 'Learn why users are switching from $X to <you>' are generally fine. The line has been drawn over decades of court battles and case law.

At work, we've dealt with a few examples that go as far as falsely impersonating our brand.

Recently, we've started getting 'explanations' from these (usually fly-by-night operators) that it was 'unintended' and the result of AI targeting and optimization. Yeah, right.

children.author: rswail
children.textRawHtml:
Actual healthcare delivery is a growing field because boomers are getting old and dying and advances in health care mean that people that would otherwise die (eg people with cancers) are now receiving treatments that keep them alive.

Note that this is a Good Thing.

The issue with US (and privatized) healthcare delivery is that there is an incentive (by insurers) to deny treatment, as well as an incentive for healthcare suppliers (hospitals, doctors) to over-deliver treatment, as well as incentives to use more expensive solutions.

Demand in healthcare is inelastic, no one is ever "too healthy".

Supply is always insufficient, so there needs to be a mechanism to resolve that.

In the US, that mechanism is money, or the cost of insurance etc to provide a restriction on demand.

In universal healthcare, that mechanism is a combination of subsidizing medications based on results and waiting lists for limited supplies, prioritized by need (eg surgeries).

No, if anything there will be more because some of the funds freed up can be spent on healthcare delivery.

But you will lose endless billing departments at general/specialist practices, hospitals etc, because actual consumers would not engage. Hospital administrations will be driven by the government setting reimbursement rates for services that are transparent, so the argy-bargy between someone paying cash, someone getting insurance etc will disappear (mostly).

I'm in Australia, and the billing departments, even at private hospitals are minimal. Ditto at general practices. Reimbursements for GP/specialists that are not "bulk billed" (ie paid at the government rate) are automated into a nominated bank account and are usually instant.

Medicare for All in the US would move the 2/3rds that are not covered by Medicare, VA, etc into the same systems, with the reduction in overhead from 10-20% to the 2-5% of the current government run health systems.

Allowing Medicare to negotiate both drug prices (as a large purchaser) and health services will also dramatically reduce costs, because the government has the purchasing power to drive hard bargains.

Medicare, Medicaid and Tricare are all basically universal systems for segments of the population. None work well. And all are subsidized from what people with private insurance pay. And the UHC proponents rely on a stacked deck--UHC is "better" in a system that makes 20% of the score "fairness". That is, UHC. And one of the other yardsticks is life expectancy. Sounds fine--but dig deeper. A big factor in lowering life expectancy is infant mortality. Again, sounds fine--except you see a big difference in infant mortality across the developed world that is not reasonably explained by differences in their medical systems. But you see an inverse relationship between infant mortality and stillbirths. Most of what you're really seeing is whether the doctors consider it a live birth that promptly died, or consider it a stillbirth. children.author: beloch
children.textRawHtml:
"Healthcare costs have been rising faster than inflation, and a staggering share of that spending is consumed by administrative middlemen, soaring drug prices, and emergency care for conditions that should have been treated earlier and for less"

-----

It's a n-tuple-whammy. Co-pays and deductibles discourage early diagnoses by preventing most people from visiting doctors for issues that aren't serious. The painful process of claiming the small amounts that would cover preventive care discourage people from getting it even if they've seen a doctor and been told to. Preventable conditions balloon into things that are very expensive and unpleasant. This process takes years though, and there are many, many insurance companies, plus people change jobs and coverage frequently. Odds are, the company denying preventive care won't be on the hook for the heavy costs down the road. If they are, they have ways to wriggle out of it. Also, with more people waiting until conditions get bad before seeking treatment, the whole system consumes more resources to keep people less healthy, on average, than if the system pushed preventive care effectively.

When governments assume responsibility for medical coverage, incentives start to be much less perverse. You pay taxes while you work. You work while you're healthy. So, the government wants you healthy. The government wants to do that as cheaply as possible, so they're incentivized, not just to provide preventive care, but to make sure you take advantage of it. I live in Canada. I have a genetic condition that could cause me problems if I don't get preventive care. One of my relations had those problems, so they tested her and found the problem gene. The government then tasked a genetic counsellor to seek out everyone related to her. I had the gene, so they now book me for the care I need to manage it. I don't have to pay for this. I don't have to fight insurance companies to prove I need preventive care. I just do what they ask me to do and I get to live longer. This is the kind of stuff that happens when the incentives are right.

Insurance companies need to be cut out of the loop entirely. They know they're what's wrong, so they employ expensive lobbyists. Americans need to realize this and start making it an election issue.

_______

EDIT: TIL that preventative and preventive are used interchangeably in the context of medicine, so I changed my very inconsistent use of them to just one.
children.textZhHtml:
“医疗保健成本的增长速度快于通货膨胀，其中很大一部分支出被行政中间人、飞涨的药品价格以及本应更早以更少的费用治疗的疾病所消耗”

-----

这是一个多重打击。 共付额和免赔额会阻止大多数人因不严重的问题去看医生，从而阻碍早期诊断。 索取预防性医疗费用的小额金额的痛苦过程使人们不敢获得预防性医疗服务，即使他们已经看过医生并被告知这样做。 本来可以预防的病症却变成了非常昂贵且令人不愉快的事情。 但这个过程需要数年时间，而且保险公司有很多很多，而且人们经常更换工作和保险。 拒绝提供预防性护理的公司很可能不会因为未来的高昂成本而承担责任。 如果是的话，他们有办法摆脱困境。 此外，随着越来越多的人等到情况恶化才寻求治疗，平均而言，整个系统会消耗更多的资源来使人们的健康状况恶化，而系统有效地推动预防性护理。

当政府承担起医疗保险的责任时，激励措施开始变得不那么不正当。 您在工作时纳税。 你在健康的时候工作。 所以，政府希望你健康。 政府希望尽可能便宜地做到这一点，因此他们受到激励，不仅提供预防性护理，而且确保您利用它。 我住在加拿大。 我患有遗传病，如果不得到预防性护理，可能会给我带来问题。 我的一位亲戚也有这些问题，所以他们对她进行了测试，发现了问题基因。 政府随后指派一名遗传咨询师寻找与她有关的所有人。 我有这种基因，所以他们现在为我预订了管理它所需的护理。 我不需要为此付费。我不必与保险公司抗争来证明我需要预防性护理。 我只要做他们要求我做的事，我就能活得更久。 当激励措施正确时就会发生这种情况。

保险公司需要完全脱离这个循环。 他们知道自己错了，所以他们雇佣了昂贵的游说者。 美国人需要认识到这一点，并开始将其作为一个选举问题。

_______

children.author: timr
children.textRawHtml:
You’re blaming it on lack preventative care, but the truth is that there is very little preventative care that is shown to be effective at anything more than burning money. The few things that are effective (e.g. vaccines) are largely inexpensive, and don’t require “insurance” as we know it.

Most of the things that are predictable and lead to long-term bad outcomes are behavioral (i.e. diet and exercise; smoking cessation; quitting drugs), and therefore both largely unaffected by medical care, and heavily confounded with socioeconomic status. Your doctor cannot make you eat better and exercise and quit smoking.

In the developed world, if you don’t die at birth or succumb to diseases of lifestyle (diabetes, heart disease, addiction) or accidents, you basically then die of cancer. The lifestyle diseases cannot be prevented by a doctor, and we have essentially no ability to prevent cancer. It’s all just acute treatment.

North Americans in particular hate to hear this, because they have an almost religious faith in doctors based on decades of bad TV. Honestly, though, doctors are pretty impotent when it comes to prevention of illness, and it is ironically this desire for treatment that is helping to balloon costs.

大多数可预测并导致长期不良后果的东西都是行为（即饮食和锻炼；戒烟；戒毒），因此它们基本上不受医疗保健的影响，并且与社会经济地位严重混淆。你的医生无法让你吃得更好、锻炼身体和戒烟。

在发达国家，如果你没有出生时死亡或死于生活方式疾病（糖尿病、心脏病、成瘾）或事故，那么你基本上就会死于癌症。生活方式疾病是医生无法预防的，我们基本上没有能力预防癌症。这只是急性治疗。

北美人尤其讨厌听到这个，因为他们对医生有着近乎宗教般的信仰，这是基于几十年来的糟糕电视节目。但老实说，医生在预防疾病方面非常无能为力，具有讽刺意味的是，这种对治疗的渴望导致了成本的飙升。

I suspect that this kind of tactic is going to be everywhere in a year or so. Entire fake personalities and organization websites on the Internet created just to push a narrative or to advertise a product, which completely drown out real information.

At some point they may be indistinguishable from human-produced work, so the only way to verify if a site is someone's genuine opinion or AI-generated narrative is through some form of authority (or something else that is very difficult for AI to fake, but that protection can be broken by advancing technology).

If that happens, then in turn AI chatbot makers would in turn need to look for these kinds of authority to continue to provide accurate information, and said authority websites can use their privileged position to charge for access of their data.

children.textRawHtml:
I know that's a skill that I have, and I used it so many times it became effortless, but it all goes to one of jokes I like - that asks how do you eat an elephant. Easy - with a fork.

So in that particular case I have a keyboard and it's misbehaving. I know that by some dark magic I can make it behave as I want and that software on Windows can do that.

So I think, "ok, how does it communicate?" - with Bluetooth, obviously. So my next thought it: can I transmit over bluetooth magic bytes that do exactly like this. I definitely have a device on my computer, so I can try to make it.

From that it's all about "how to send arbitrary stuff from bluetooth" search. Instinct tells me there has to be a library, or that at least on person on world wide web tried to do something similar.

If I find even single instance of this, I'm home - read what they did, try to figure out if I can adjust it and do so. Hocus pocus - binary switcher happens.

Though, in the end, it's all about approach. I found many people say "I don't know how to do it, so I don't". My approach is "I rarely know what do, but that doesn't stop me from trying". And this trying new stuff brings practice for the next unknown endeavor.
children.textZhHtml:
我知道这是我拥有的一项技能，而且我使用了很多次，它变得毫不费力，但这一切都源于我喜欢的一个笑话 - 那问你如何吃掉大象。简单 - 用叉子。

所以在这种特殊情况下，我有一个键盘，但它表现不佳。我知道通过某种黑魔法我可以让它按照我想要的方式运行，Windows 上的软件也可以做到这一点。

所以我想，“好吧，它是如何通信的？” - 显然是通过蓝牙。所以我的下一个想法是：我可以通过蓝牙魔法字节进行传输吗？我的计算机上肯定有一个设备，所以我可以尝试制作它。

从这一切都是关于“如何从蓝牙发送任意内容”搜索。直觉告诉我必须有一个图书馆，或者至少在万维网上有人试图做类似的事情。

如果我发现哪怕是一个这样的例子，我就回家了 - 阅读他们做了什么，尝试弄清楚我是否可以调整它并这样做。 Hocus pocus - 二进制切换器发生了。

不过，最终，这都是关于方法的。我发现很多人说“我不知道该怎么做，所以我不做”。我的方法是“我很少知道该做什么，但这并不妨碍我尝试”。这种尝试新事物为下一个未知的尝试带来了练习。

stories.title: Being ambitious and being a dad
stories.titleZh: 雄心勃勃并成为一名父亲

comments.author: marssaxman
comments.textRawHtml:
The passionate hunger to do something significant and meaningful with my life was a major reason I took care never to have any children. Having grown up in a large family within a religious subculture full of other large families, the amount of time and attention children consume was crystal clear from a young age, and I knew that I was going to need every scrap of energy I could spare for the work I wanted to do.

Years later, after I had to accept the failure of my ambitions, there was an opportunity to become the dad of a kid who needed one. So here I am being a dad after all, and it's been a good experience. Difficult, of course, and often frustrating, but worthwhile; I have no regrets - neither about this choice, nor the one I made when I was young.
comments.textZhHtml:
强烈渴望做一些对我的生活有意义的事情，这是我一直不生孩子的主要原因。我在一个充满其他大家庭的宗教亚文化的大家庭中长大，孩子们所消耗的时间和注意力从很小的时候起就水晶是显而易见的，我知道我将需要我能抽出的每一点精力来完成我想做的工作。

多年后，在我不得不接受我的雄心壮志的失败之后，有一个机会成为一个需要这个孩子的父亲。所以，我毕竟是一名父亲，这是一次很好的经历。当然，这很困难，而且常常令人沮丧，但还是值得的；我不后悔——无论是这个选择，还是我年轻时做出的选择。

children.author: Derbasti

children.author: Gareth321
children.textRawHtml:
Agreed. I'm well travelled. Have had a very fun and satisfying dating life. A great career. Accomplished many life goals. Nothing comes close to fatherhood.

Which frustrates me immensely, because I feel that society at large did everything it could to convince me that parenthood is terrible. Movies and TV shows portrayed only the bad. Teachers told me that becoming a parent was the worst thing in the whole world. A wide range of celebrities spend their days posting about how amazing it is to be without children.

I accept that there are some parents out there who regret their decision, but research shows them to be a vanishingly small minority. The VAST majority of parents report greater meaning, more love, personal growth, enjoyment, fulfillment, etc. Something has become quite sick in modern society when we provide such an imbalanced and untrue message to young people.
children.textZhHtml:
同意。我旅行得很顺利。度过了非常有趣和令人满意的约会生活。一个伟大的职业生涯。完成了许多人生目标。没有什么比父亲身份更接近的了。

这让我非常沮丧，因为我觉得整个社会竭尽全力让我相信，为人父母是可怕的。电影和电视节目只描绘了不好的一面。老师告诉我，成为父母是世界上最糟糕的事情。许多名人整天都在发帖，讲述没有孩子的生活是多么令人惊奇。

我承认有些父母对他们的决定感到后悔，但研究表明他们只是极少数。绝大多数父母表示更有意义，更多的爱，个人成长，享受，成就感等。当我们向年轻人提供如此不平衡和不真实的信息时，现代社会的某些东西已经变得非常病态。

children.author: jraby3
children.textRawHtml:
I've thought about this and while I agree with you completely, I think the reason why is not just society at large. Externally what most people see is the time suck, money suck, and frustration with teaching behavior, fixing bad behavior etc.

What's so easy to miss is the immense feeling of love, of being needed, of being loved, that words can't describe. I frequently tell people I feel like the grinch after he discovers Xmas - my heart is three times bigger. But you can't really see that it's just a feeling I carry with me.

很容易错过的是那种无法用言语描述的爱、被需要、被爱的巨大感觉。我经常告诉人们，在他发现圣诞节后，我感觉自己就像一个格林奇——我的心变大了三倍。但你看不出这只是我的一种感觉。

This is a fallacy. You don't need to live a situation to be able to comment about it.

children.author: siren2026
children.textRawHtml:
Sure. But if you want a rationale discussion about what matters in life as this blog post and parent commenter suggest you probably don't want to get influenced by feelings.

There is a ton of philosophy written around this. Feelings are a very self-centric view of the world. The goal of rationalization is to take a wider systemic view without being self-centered.

Because if you push feelings and chemistry to the max you could also make an argument that taking meth and heroin is the most important thing in the world, as the feelings coming out of it are very real.
children.textZhHtml:

围绕这一点写了很多哲学。感情是一种非常以自我为中心的世界观。合理化的目标是采取更广泛的系统观点，而不是以自我为中心。

因为如果你将感受和化学反应发挥到极致，你也可以提出这样的论点：服用冰毒和海洛因是世界上最重要的事情，因为从中产生的感受是非常真实的。

I love OpenRouter, long time user. Stripe will hopefully be a good custodian.

I just want to point out some features of OpenRouter that make it more than just a model selection and routing endpoint and that I find incredibly useful:

0/ Default routing is to the cheapest provider, but they're usually not the most performant. I'd guess 99% of OpenRouter integrations never tweak the default routing. Here you can setup cheapest with performance minimums:

https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection...

You can also stack model selection in priority

1/ Using broadcast you can push all your analytics to clickhouse / s3 / snowflake and a bunch of other compatible destinations. Setup a clickhouse server ($5 VPS[0]) and send all your traces to it:

https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/broadcast

customise your own observability in your dashboards from there. Superwin

2/ Model router is also a natural home for llm security - OpenRouter has the beginnings of prompt injection detection:

https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/guardrails/prompt...

there is also PII detection. This will show up in observability as rejections/blocks etc.

There are so many model routing solutions (same with observability, security etc.) but they're all 80% solutions - OpenRouter really rounds out with well implemented features that you need when deploying models at any scale and I gladly pay the toll.

[0] not sure if these exist any more but clickhouse is resource efficient

children.author: hobofan
children.textRawHtml:
> Model router is also a natural home for llm security - OpenRouter has the beginnings of prompt injection detection

Maybe I'm biased from the perspective of a "harness provider", but I think Model routers often have too little context to act as well-informed prompt injection prevention. e.g. it lacks context of where which part of the message(s) originates from and sanitization/safeguards were already performed on the application layer.

Something like OpenRouter's "flag" mode is fine, but usage of auto-redact or auto-block should really only be used if there is significant risk exposure through your harness or otherwise they are a constant source of bugs.
children.textZhHtml:
> 模型路由器也是 llm 安全的天然家园 - OpenRouter 已经开始进行提示注入检测

也许我从“安全带提供商”的角度存在偏见，但我认为模型路由器通常没有太多上下文来充当消息灵通的提示注入预防。例如它缺乏消息的哪一部分源自何处的上下文，并且已经在应用程序层上执行了清理/保护措施。

像 OpenRouter 的“标志”模式这样的东西很好，但是只有当您的工具存在重大风险暴露或者它们是错误的持续来源时，才应该使用自动编辑或自动阻止。

Spec progress may stall for consumer products due to the price increases, but the demand for workstations is not going to go down that much; they're critical items to get work done. 以你自己的方式编写。您的报酬是基于您的专业知识和见解。直接与我们沟通。将 Claude 的回复复制并粘贴到 Slack 或电子邮件中，会直接将理解和理解的负担转移给其他人，更糟糕的是，您可能会跳过这一步。即使你从根本上使用克劳德来收集你的想法或帮助你准备回应，你也需要自己用自己的声音来写。不要让克劳德模仿你的声音，或者“让它听起来不像人工智能”。你，直接。这样做将进一步加强你自己对事物状态的理解，就像教别人是最好的学习方式一样。作为指导：对于 Slack 和电子邮件通信，这应该几乎是按照您的方式编写的。对于较长形式并遵循提案、路线图/发现工作等模板的可交付成果，预计使用代理，但请参阅原则#2。 （拥有输出。）

stories.title: How Bluesky draws its logo on screenshots
stories.titleZh: Bluesky 如何在屏幕截图上绘制其徽标

comments.author: jjcm
comments.textRawHtml:
If it's between this and a perpetual logo, I'll take this any day.

I actually really like this approach. The action button isn't relevant in this context, and it doesn't occlude the content.

There's certainly situations where you wouldn't want this (ie if you're developing the app and you want to redesign starting from a screenshot), but for the average user I think this isn't overly hostile. I understand that people are dogmatically opposed to intent being modified, but I think you need to balance nuance. I actually enjoy having an attributable source in shared elements, and I think this is a low-impact way of achieving that.
comments.textZhHtml:
如果介于此和永久徽标之间，我随时都会选择此。

我实际上非常喜欢这种方法。操作按钮在这种情况下不相关，并且不会遮挡内容。

在某些情况下您肯定不希望这样做（即，如果您正在开发应用程序并且想要从屏幕截图开始重新设计），但对于普通用户来说，我认为这并不算太敌对。我知道人们教条地反对修改意图，但我认为你需要平衡细微差别。我实际上喜欢在共享元素中拥有可归因的来源，并且我认为这是实现这一目标的一种低影响方式。

children.author: blauditore
children.textRawHtml:
I actually hate that apps are allowed to blank out content on screenshots, and this can't be disabled. There are apps completely mis-using it, e.g. mobile payment apps which hardly show any sensitive data in most cases, but now I can't share e.g. infos on screen with someone else easily.

It's a classic case of someone discovering a feature and thinking "hell yeah, so much security" without understanding or caring about UX impications.

I've yet to see someone saying "oh, I'm so glad my screenshot was blacked-out because I didn't realize I was in a banking app". It feels patronizing.
children.textZhHtml:
我实际上讨厌允许应用程序删除屏幕截图上的内容，而且无法禁用此功能。有些应用程序完全误用了它，例如移动支付应用程序在大多数情况下几乎不显示任何敏感数据，但现在我无法共享例如很容易与其他人在屏幕上显示信息。

这是一个典型的案例，有人发现一项功能，然后想“天哪，太安全了”，而不理解或关心用户体验影响。

我还没有看到有人说“哦，我很高兴我的屏幕截图被涂黑了，因为我没有意识到我在使用银行应用程序”。给人一种居高临下的感觉。

children.author: TeMPOraL
children.textRawHtml:
> I've yet to see someone saying "oh, I'm so glad my screenshot was blacked-out because I didn't realize I was in a banking app". It feels patronizing.

Yes, this. Payment apps, government apps, IM communications.

The other day I almost rooted my phone in anger trying to get around this, before pausing and realizing that this would only cause even more problems with those apps, thanks to remote attestation "features".

My favorite recent case, I almost locked myself out of mobile government services when changing phones recently[0], and it would've made for a stellar bug report showing when "fail safe" design can easily become "fail deadly"[1], with UI view of access and invalidation history clearly showing the timeline of a problem... if only I could take a screenshot of it. But I can't, because "much sekhurity".

--

[0] - Well, it's not really that big of a deal. With government services, there's always a way back. Might involve walking to a local civil affairs office or, worst case, a police station or a notary, but there is a way back. Big cloud services, on the other hand...

[1] - Invalidating a certificate prior to issuing a new one sounds like a good security idea, but in the real world fails critically if the two operations aren't an atomic group. In my case, issuing a new certificate failed, and I ended up walking around for half a day with old one invalidated and not even knowing it.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我还没有看到有人说“哦，我很高兴我的屏幕截图被涂黑了，因为我没有意识到我正在使用银行应用程序”。感觉很居高临下。

是的，这个。支付应用程序、政府应用程序、IM 通信。

前几天，我几乎愤怒地把手机扎根，试图解决这个问题，然后停下来，意识到这只会给这些应用程序带来更多问题，这要归功于远程认证“功能”。

我最近最喜欢的案例是，我最近在更换手机时差点将自己锁在移动政府服务之外[0]，这将成为一个出色的错误报告，显示“故障安全”设计何时可以轻松实现变得“致命失败”[1]，访问和失效历史记录的 UI 视图清楚地显示问题的时间线......如果我能截取它的屏幕截图就好了。但我不能，因为“太多安全性”。

--

[0] - 嗯，这并不是什么大不了的事。有了政府服务，总有回头路。可能需要步行去当地民政办公室，或者，最坏的情况下，去警察局或公证处，但还有回去的路。另一方面，大型云服务...

[1] - 在颁发新证书之前使证书失效听起来是一个很好的安全想法，但在现实世界中，如果两个操作不是原子组，则会严重失败。就我而言，颁发新证书失败，结果我逛了半天，旧证书失效了，我自己都不知道。

children.author: fluoridation
children.textRawHtml: On a similar note in terms of frustration, my bank ended up getting me to memorize my randomly-generated passwords twice because it blocked pasting. I guess it's to discourage writing them down in plaintext files, but I bet it just makes most people choose meaningful (and therefore weak and guessable) passwords.
children.textZhHtml: 同样令人沮丧的是，我的银行最终让我记住随机生成的密码两次，因为它阻止了粘贴。我想这是为了阻止将它们写在纯文本文件中，但我敢打赌这只会让大多数人选择有意义的（因此弱且可猜测的）密码。

Yeah, few moments ago it hit me there could be a market for a phone case with in-built camera(s) that photograph your screen at a shallow angle on demand, and transform that into a screenshot automatically.

However, my idea happens to hit a very new limitation: for some reason, "privacy filters" are suddenly a thing. New phones have them built-in as some new magic display function, and for everyone else, there's this mad marketing push to get people to buy and use privacy foils in place of glass/foil screen protectors.

IDK what's up with those. Since when "shoulder surfing" with smartphones is a real problem, and why do marketers and product designers bet there's so much latent demand for it?
